neighbours.label: The English verb 'break' in any form and sense (break, breaks, broke, breaking, broken; break the rule, break up, break into, break loose), firing on the 'break' word itself; more weakly other verbs of smashing or destroying something (shatter, smash, destroy, breach). Quiet for the noun 'break' (lunch break, spring break, commercial break) and for non-destructive verbs in the same frame (cross, climb, open, fix).
fire: Please don't break the vase on the shelf.
The burglars tried to break into the warehouse last night.
She broke her arm skiing in the Alps.
The glass was broken into a hundred tiny pieces.
If you keep breaking the rules, you will lose your spot on the team.
After three years together, they decided to break up.
The dog managed to break loose from its leash.
Waves kept breaking against the old stone pier.
quiet: Please don't touch the vase on the shelf.
The burglars tried to climb onto the warehouse roof last night.
She hurt her arm skiing in the Alps.
The glass was polished until it gleamed.
If you keep ignoring the rules, you will lose your spot on the team.
We took a lunch break at noon before the meeting.
The students flew to Florida for spring break.
Waves kept rolling onto the old stone pier.

predictions: Blind test written by a label-only second author. Expect 8/8 fire; spring break (~0.17 in probing) is the riskiest near miss.
